'''''Impatiens niamniamensis''''', common name '''Congo cockatoo''', '''parrot impatiens''' or simply '''parrot plant''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Balsaminaceae]].

==Description==
''Impatiens niamniamensis'' grows about {{convert|60|-|90|cm}} long. This evergreen, perennial species has an erect, succulent, brown stem resembling wood. Leaves are simple, ovate-oblong or elliptical, spirally arranged, about 10 cm long.

This plant produces bright and colourful bird-shaped flowers (hence the common names ''Congo cockatoo'' and ''parrot plant'') with a long, curled nectar spur. These unusual flowers vary in colour and size, but those of the clone most common in cultivation in Europe and America ('African Princess') are usually scarlet red and yellow and can reach a length of about {{convert|3.5|cm}}. Fruits are explosive  capsules of about 14–16 mm.
[[File:Balsaminaceae - Impatiens niamniamensis.JPG|thumb|240px|center|Close-up on a flower of ''Impatiens niamniamensis'']]

== Etymology ==
The epithet ''niamniamensis'' comes from the [[onomatopoeic]] name Niam-Niam which is sometimes used for the [[Azande people]] who live in the south-eastern part of the [[Central African Republic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NParks {{!}} Impatiens niamniamensis |url=https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/6/2/6277 |access-date=2023-10-28 |website=www.nparks.gov.sg}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Impatiens niamniamensis'' comes from tropical Africa. It can be found from Cameroon throughout tropical Africa, up to Sudan and down to the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]].<ref name=POWO_103811-1>{{citation |title=''Impatiens niamniamensis'' Gilg |work=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:103811-1 |accessdate=2020-07-03 }}</ref> It grows in moist and shaded bushlands, at an elevation of {{convert|350|-|2400|m}} above sea level.

==Cultivation==
This plant is widely cultivated. In [[temperate climate|temperate]] zones it requires protection from temperatures below {{convert| 10|C|F|abbr=on}}. It needs a sheltered position in a partially shaded spot. ''Impatiens niamniamensis'' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]. <ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/9151/Impatiens-niamniamensis/Details | title = ''Impatiens niamniamensis'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 21 September 2020}}</ref>
